contributions.statement: Do not front routine, short agent tasks with an LLM-grown task DAG and parallel workers: on tasks a single agent finished in under about 1M tokens, the DAG version was slower and used roughly 9-15x the tokens.
contributions.evidence: §4.1 Table 1: on Cybench Direct finishes sooner on 30/40 tasks, mean 7.31 vs 8.49 min and 0.83M vs 3.22M tokens. Table 2: strata <0.1M and 0.1-1M Direct tokens give mean time ratios 0.42 and 0.66 (Cairn slower) and token ratios 14.71x and 8.66x. Same base agent (Pi) and model; Cairn swaps in role prompts, graph tools and up to six slots, so the overhead source is not isolated. Strata are defined by Direct's own tokens and Cybench is a single run (audit).
relative_to: 2605.15425 fine-grained LLM task decomposition triples tokens with no correctness gain

contributions.statement: Consider a planner-grown task DAG with parallel workers only for long tasks (a single agent needing more than ~1M tokens or ~45 minutes), where it roughly halved wall-clock time at ~3.7x tokens, and compare it first against N independent single agents run in parallel at the same token budget.
contributions.evidence: Table 2, >=1M stratum (17 tasks, 29 runs): mean time 47.20 -> 25.35 min, per-task token ratio 3.69x. §4.3 Fig. 8: on one FrontierMath problem, 1/3/6 slots took 97.2/73.7/26.5 min. Wall-clock compares six execution slots against one and is not normalized; no parallel independent-agent baseline; FrontierMath uses the twelve public sample problems (audit).
relative_to: 2605.15425 decomposition pays only when failures and retries are frequent
2609.38345 best-of-N single-agent baseline at equal tokens before crediting multi-agent structure

reason: The low-effort penalty is a same-agent, same-model comparison and gives a usable cost boundary for LLM-generated task DAGs; the high-effort time gain is confounded by six-versus-one execution slots and lacks a parallel baseline, so it stays a hypothesis.
